evals.prompt: Our team estimates the data-platform migration will take 9 months. Before it goes on the roadmap, sanity-check that with an outside view — what does a reference class of similar migration projects say about how long these actually take?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Defines the forecast quantity and unit (schedule in months, or actual/planned ratio) and records the inside view as stated; Proposes 2-3 candidate reference classes and justifies the choice on the similarity vs sample-size trade-off; Assembles the class's outcome distribution with sources and n, reporting P10/P50/P80/P90 rather than the mean; Positions the 9-month estimate as a percentile of the class and interprets it; Computes the uplift to a target percentile (P50/P80) and adjusts only with specific, evidenced reasons; Reports base rate, percentile, uplift and residual inside-view adjustment with rationale using the output template.
expectations: Defines the forecast quantity and unit (schedule in months, or actual/planned ratio) and records the inside view as stated
Proposes 2-3 candidate reference classes and justifies the choice on the similarity vs sample-size trade-off
Assembles the class's outcome distribution with sources and n, reporting P10/P50/P80/P90 rather than the mean
Positions the 9-month estimate as a percentile of the class and interprets it
Computes the uplift to a target percentile (P50/P80) and adjusts only with specific, evidenced reasons
Reports base rate, percentile, uplift and residual inside-view adjustment with rationale using the output template

evals.prompt: What's the base rate for enterprise software rollouts finishing within their original budget? I want the outside view before I trust the internal estimate of $2.4M.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Treats the question as a reference-class exercise: names the class of comparable rollouts and its outcome distribution (cost-overrun ratios), with sources and n; Locates the $2.4M inside estimate as a percentile of the class rather than accepting or rejecting it outright; States the uplift required to reach a P50 or P80 forecast and flags any small-n caveat.
expectations: Treats the question as a reference-class exercise: names the class of comparable rollouts and its outcome distribution (cost-overrun ratios), with sources and n
Locates the $2.4M inside estimate as a percentile of the class rather than accepting or rejecting it outright
States the uplift required to reach a P50 or P80 forecast and flags any small-n caveat

evals.prompt: Apply reference class forecasting to this R&D budget: the inside-view estimate is EUR 1.2M and here are cost-overrun ratios from 12 comparable programmes.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Runs the procedure: quantity and unit, class description with n = 12, distribution percentiles (type-7 quantiles via the companion tool), position of the inside view, uplift to the target percentile; Adjusts the class-based forecast only for specific, evidenced differences and states the adjustment multiplier; Uses the output template and reports the final P50/P80 forecast in EUR.
expectations: Runs the procedure: quantity and unit, class description with n = 12, distribution percentiles (type-7 quantiles via the companion tool), position of the inside view, uplift to the target percentile
Adjusts the class-based forecast only for specific, evidenced differences and states the adjustment multiplier
Uses the output template and reports the final P50/P80 forecast in EUR

evals.prompt: I currently put 40% on the vendor shipping on time; their latest status report says the beta slipped two weeks. Update my probability given this new evidence.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Performs a Bayes-factor update of a single belief (prior, likelihood ratio, posterior) rather than assembling a reference class distribution.
expectations: Performs a Bayes-factor update of a single belief (prior, likelihood ratio, posterior) rather than assembling a reference class distribution
